messages.subject: Registering brains
parts:
Dear Adam,

On 16 Jul 2015, at 7:04, Adam Claridge-Chang wrote:

> I'm curious about how to register our own brains to a reference brain,
> is that something done in NAT, FIJI or VFB?

You can see bit.ly/flybrains for templates. FCWB is the template used
for FlyCircuit data, but I recommend JFRC2 if you have nc82 stained
brains.

For registration you can try https://github.com/jefferis/fiji-cmtk-gui
NB this only tested on a mac unfortunately. I recommend the Cachero 2010
registration parameters.

You can read much more about this in a CSH protocols articles that they
seem to have divided into 3

http://cshprotocols.cshlp.org/content/2013/4/pdb.prot071712.short

the staining and image registration ones are what you want. Note however
that the image registration GUI has been superseded by the one linked
above.

Best wishes,

Greg.

Sent from my iPad

> On 18 Jul 2015, at 08:55, Adam Claridge-Chang <ada...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> One snag is that our nc82 attempts never worked, so we use DLG.

You can use the FCWB template.

> Marta mentioned there might be a bridging registration using double-stained DLG/nc82 brains?

There is a bridging reg but it's not perfect since it was not based on a double stained brain. However we have used it extensively.

> If not, or if you think the results won't be so good we will order some Chemtag lines from Bloomington and try your method to get good BRP patterns.

Of course I can recommend these. But if you try the Janelia fly light 5d nc82 protocol it should work. Best,

Greg b
